communities.title: LIDAR/DIAL TECHNIQUES APPLICATIONS
communities.summary: Lidar and DIAL techniques serve as primary methods for mapping aerosol distributions, topography with centimeter-level resolution, and tree canopies.

communities.title: LIDAR System Requirements and Techniques
communities.summary: The community describes LIDAR techniques as requiring pulsed lasers and large aperture telescopes. DIAL is a specific technique within this domain that further requires tunable, monochromatic lasers with high spectral purity. Aerosol mapping is identified as a simple application utilizing relatively small systems (few Kg) with modest energy (~100W).

communities.title: UAV/MAV Ecosystem: Platforms, Missions, and Technologies
communities.summary: The community defines a diverse ecosystem of Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) ranging from Micro Air Vehicles (MAVs) to High-Altitude Mother Ships. These platforms operate under various supervision models (Ground-Based, Lead Aircraft, Mother Ship) to execute missions spanning disaster assessment, atmospheric profiling, and covert operations. Key capabilities include Formation Flight for synchronized sensor operations, Over-The-Horizon (OTH) communication for C2, and advanced autonomy software for optimal flight planning. Technical challenges involve miniaturization using MEMS devices, managing conflicting altitude requirements (low-level urban to high-altitude tropopause), and ensuring system reliability through Fault Detection, Isolation, and Recovery (FDIR) technologies like Livingstone.

nodes: OPERATOR OF UAS (OPERADOR DE SISTEMAS AÉREOS NO TRIPULADOS)
UAS SCHOOL (ESCUELA DE UAS DE LAS FAS)
communities.title: CLASS I-III UAVs Community Report
communities.summary: The community comprises three distinct UAV classes (I, II, III) characterized by varying operational scopes, procurement programs, and statistical performance metrics. Key relationships include the UAS School providing training for Class I and II operators, active inventory counts across 95 countries, and specific acquisition plans like the Polish Armed Forces Development Program 2013-2022. Statistical analyses reveal no correlation between Maximum Takeoff Weight (MTOW) and performance metrics such as velocity or ceiling altitude.

communities.title: Class I Multirotor UAV Scaling and Design Analysis
communities.summary: The community centers on Class I multirotor UAVs, where geometric parameters (wheelbase, propeller diameter) and performance metrics (battery capacity) scale predictably with Maximum Take-Off Weight (MTOW). The analysis relies on a specific database containing 161 entries for battery data and 55 for wheelbase, utilizing power-law regressions to estimate missing values. Key findings include the sub-linear scaling of structural dimensions relative to mass and the significant influence of mission requirements like endurance and range on battery sizing.

communities.title: UAV Payload and System Specifications Report
communities.summary: The dataset details payload configurations for commercial multirotor UAVs, specifically the Yamaha RMAX helicopter, including weight (30 kg), volume (0.5 m³), power requirements (3-5 kW), and specific sensor suites like hyper-spectral sensors and LIDAR. It highlights discrepancies between predicted and actual performance metrics for certain models (e.g., Lumenier Defender) and notes limitations in electric motor sustainability for payload missions.

communities.title: Class II Multirotor Sizing and Scaling Analysis
communities.summary: The report details the sizing framework for Class II multirotors, focusing on scaling laws between Maximum Take-Off Weight (MTOW) and critical parameters like battery mass and energy. Key findings include statistical ranges for battery mass (0.30–20.00 kg), energy capacity (15.84–4560 Wh), and specific regression metrics (AAII, BII, ENII, etc.) derived from datasets of varying sizes. The analysis distinguishes between payload categories (≤50 kg vs >50 kg) and utilizes physics-based analysis for refinement after initial estimates.

communities.title: Early Rotorcraft Studies: Lorenz, Omri & Rand
communities.summary: The community centers on early rotorcraft analyses by Lorenz and supplementary work by Omri & Rand. Lorenz focused on autogyros and single-rotor helicopters with thermal-powered configurations, deriving power-law regressions linking installed power, rotor radius, and MTOW using piston or turboshaft engines. Omri & Rand supplemented the dataset with non-dimensional similarity coefficients, also emphasizing autogyros and single-rotor helicopters.

communities.title: Heavy Lift Multirotor Design Analysis
communities.summary: The Heavy Lift Multirotor is a Class II coaxial UAV with an estimated MTOW of 130.09 kg, featuring 8 rotors each with a diameter of 1.09 m. Its physical dimensions are 3.5 m in length and 3.6 m in breadth, supported by an estimated battery mass of 18.5 kg. Design variables such as rotor count, per-motor loading, and actuator disk area critically influence structural requirements, motor selection, and overall energy consumption.

communities.title: UAV Class II Design and Scaling Analysis
communities.summary: Class II UAVs (MTOW 150–600 kg) are defined by near-linear or super-linear scaling behaviors driven by actuator area (AA). AA, calculated via Equation. 10 [c_c80e6bc4fc0d4314800d70cc], governs disc loading and directly influences thrust generation, rotor efficiency, and aerodynamic efficiency [c_5816e0cf358bc096ed27040e]. Design thrust per motor is derived from calculated hover requirements (e.g., 13.6 kgf/motor × 1.5 safety factor = 20.4 kgf) using regression coefficients (α) and exponents (β) presented in Tables A1 and A2 [c_0f50dea6275772f4ade77901]. Models such as Searcher Mk 2, Hermes 450, Aerostar, and Dominator fall within this classification, with specific periods noted (e.g., Hermes 450: 2007–2014) [c_b0fc563fffabf0dbe43a9779]. The dataset includes 130 units exceeding 1 kg MTOW, aligning with the larger industrial multirotors industry category [c_e2a6a3efb31a7588ee14f4aa, c_0d9b79e7acd084e496f01028].

communities.title: UAV Geometric and Statistical Metrics Report
communities.summary: The community describes Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) geometric dimensions (Length, Breadth), payload categories, actuation areas, battery mass-energy relations, and statistical conditions (2σ.α, 2σ.β, 3σ.α, 3σ.β, No outlier removal). Key findings include specific dimension values for Class I/II UAVs, actual vs predicted dimensions for models like D230A, FLIR SKYRANGER, GRYPHON GD-120X, JMRRC, HF C50 AGRI, and statistical coefficients under various conditions.

communities.title: Heavy-Lift Multirotor Design and Dynamics Report
communities.summary: The report details a Class II heavy-lift multirotor UAV (MTOW 130.09 kg) designed for a 60 kg payload using an eight-rotor coaxial configuration. The vehicle's dynamics are modeled via equations of motion fed with mass and inertia parameters derived from CAD models. Control is achieved through a cascade PID structure implemented in MATLAB/Simulink Software-In-the-Loop Simulations (SILS). Key design metrics include dimensions of 3.5 m length and 3.6 m breadth, with motor efficiency peaking at 60-75% throttle.

communities.title: Maximum Takeoff Weight (MTOW) Estimates Across Aircraft Categories
communities.summary: The data presents Maximum Takeoff Weight (MTOW) estimates for various aircraft categories, including general aviation, military, and specialized types. Values are provided as three distinct estimates per category, often showing a consistent offset pattern across the dataset.

communities.title: Multirotor Design Space and Scaling Relations
communities.summary: The multirotor design space encompasses dominant trends derived from commercially available UAVs (agricultural, imaging, general purpose) alongside specific variants optimized for agility, thrust, compact heavy-lift, or high payload fractions. These scaling relations were validated via regression analysis under varying outlier removal criteria (2σ, 3σ, none), confirming robustness against data point exclusion.

communities.title: Class II UAV Database and MTOW Scaling Analysis
communities.summary: The Class II database comprises 130 multirotor UAVs with Maximum Takeoff Weight (MTOW) exceeding 1 kg, ranging from 1.05 kg to 800 kg. MTOW serves as the primary scaling variable for structural layout, actuation area, and payload capacity, exhibiting distinct behaviors below and above a 50 kg threshold. Payload mass scales linearly below 50 kg but sub-linearly above it, while energy availability increases sub-linearly with weight. Several performance parameters like maximum velocity and ceiling altitude show no statistically significant correlation with MTOW due to limited data.

communities.title: Class I 멀티로터 및 이륙 조건 분석
communities.summary: Class I 멀티로터의 중력 지표와 배터리/양력 지수는 최대 이륙 중량 (MTOWI) 에 대한 멱함수 모델 ($y = \alpha x^\beta$) 로 정의되며, 가속도 식은 중력가속도 ($g$), 마찰계수, 구조적 무게 비율 등 다양한 물리량을 포함합니다.

communities.title: Class~I UAV Community Report
communities.summary: The data defines a community of Class~I UAVs, including FPV and racing types like AOS RC V5, QAV-PRO Mirage, AcroBee75, iFlight BumbleBee, and Walkera F210. These units prioritize agility over endurance and thrust-to-weight ratio. Specific models exhibit significant discrepancies between actual and predicted performance metrics (e.g., endurance, wheelbase, propeller diameter), with some data points missing entirely. Nano-quads are also linked to FPV, imaging, and recreational applications.

communities.title: Sensor Payload Community Report
communities.summary: The sensor payload integrates a hyper-spectral sensor (5-20 m resolution), multi-spectral optical camera, SAR, LIDAR, thermal imager, digital camera, and an omnidirectional RF receiver. The system supports snow pack depth measurement objectives.

communities.title: LIDAR and Radar Platform System for River Measurement
communities.summary: The system comprises two distinct aerial platforms: a LIDAR-equipped vehicle measuring river geometry along channels, and a Radar platform measuring river height over regions of interest. The LIDAR sensor is constrained to 500W power, 7 ft³ volume, and 55 lbs weight, while the dual-frequency radar requires 1-5 kW power and up to 440 lbs weight. Both platforms require accurate position knowledge; the LIDAR platform provides real-time trajectory information to the radar system.

communities.title: Active Optical Remote Sensing Community
communities.summary: Active optical remote sensing, also known as lidar, utilizes an optical source (typically a laser) to detect hard objects such as terrain, other vehicles, and obstacles.

nodes: GEOLOGIC CONTROLS ON ICE SHEET DYNAMICS
communities.title: Autonomous Low-Cost Aircraft Platform Sensor Community
communities.summary: The community centers on an autonomous low-cost aircraft platform deploying various sensors, primarily LIDAR and magnetometers, to measure atmospheric aerosols, primary chemicals (H2O, O3, CO2), ice sheet dynamics (elevation, bed characteristics), and geologic controls. Key findings include conflicting specifications for LIDAR weight (4.4-22 lbs vs 88 lbs) and power (5-40 W vs 600 W), the use of digitized waveform methods and Fabry-Perot filters, and comparisons with passive instruments and water vapor soundings.

communities.title: Sensor Payload Community Report
communities.summary: The sensor payload community comprises a thermal imager, digital camera, multi-spectral imager, hyper-spectral imager, video camera, and GPS/INS. Key findings include current weights ranging from 1.1 lbs (0.5 kg) for the digital camera to 15.4 lbs (7 kg) for the hyper-spectral imager, with future projections showing significant reductions in weight and volume across all components. Power requirements are estimated at less than 30 Watts for the payload excluding LIDAR.

communities.title: Long Wave Infra-Red Camera System Specifications
communities.summary: The long wave infra-red camera system is a payload component weighing approximately 33 lbs (15 kg) and consuming 20-30 watts of power. It operates at an altitude of 30,000 ft (9 km) with a 30 degree look down field of view, achieving a resolution of 3.28 ft (1 m).

nodes: TUNABLE DIODE LASER BASED INFRA-RED SPECTROMETER
communities.title: ARGUS INSTRUMENT COMMUNITY REPORT
communities.summary: The ARGUS instrument, a TRL 9 tunable diode laser-based infra-red spectrometer, is operational on the B-57 high altitude research aircraft at Johnson Space Center. While ready for UAV deployment, its current endurance is limited to 6 hours by LN2 cryogen requirements. Progress toward UAV application is constrained by strict measurement requirements limiting the number of studyable molecules and the need to reduce size, weight, and power. An enlarged dewar could extend endurance to 18 hours, and cavity ringdown technology represents a potential future solution for UAV suitability.

communities.title: Sensor Package Capabilities and Limitations
communities.summary: The sensor package integrates a hyper-spectral imager, thermal imager, digital camera, video camera, GPS/Inertial Navigation System (INS), and vegetation canopy or fluorescence LIDAR. Its utility is constrained by specific measurement capabilities regarding horizontal wind and humidity, which are noted as lacking improvement activity.

communities.title: Imager Platform Community Report
communities.summary: The Imager platform is an imaging system designed to hover or circle regions of interest, requiring station-keeping capabilities between 3,000 ft (1 km) and 82,000 ft (25 km), a transport range of 5,400 nm (10,000 km), and endurance of at least 24–48 hours (ideally one week). It necessitates an attitude accuracy of 0.1 degree and positional accuracy of 33 ft (10 m). The platform includes instruments such as a dual-pole multiple frequency microwave radar, a passive microwave imager (19–183 GHz), and smart drop-sondes. It communicates with an In Situ platform and a Storage platform, which shares the same requirements as the Imager.

communities.title: UAV Instrument Market Dynamics
communities.summary: The UAV instrument market is characterized by a dichotomy between affordable, high-performance CCD cameras and expensive, slow-to-deliver IR components.

communities.title: Endangered Maritime Species Location Mission Report
communities.summary: The mission focuses on locating and tracking endangered European tuna in the Central/Northern Atlantic Ocean using Lidar. Success depends on observing specific feeding behaviors where fish are stationary, while accounting for challenges like deep water diving that renders them undetectable. The study evaluates population counts, migration patterns, and habitat quality.

nodes: NASA CIVIL UAV CAPABILITIES ASSESSMENT TEAM

USRA CIVIL UAV TECHNOLOGY REVIEW PROJECT
communities.title: Civil UAV Technology Review Project Overview
communities.summary: The Civil UAV Technology Review Project (April-June 2006) was implemented by USRA to support the NASA Civil UAV Capabilities Assessment Team. It involved a review of 43 technology areas and 16 mission capabilities, utilizing input from 36 subject matter experts (SMEs) and academia participants. Technical Working Groups (TWGs) focused on sensor technologies like infrared, magnetometers, and spectroscopy devices to develop timelines for performance improvements, size/weight reductions, and R&D needs.

nodes: COORDINATION WITH MINI- OR MICRO- AERIAL VEHICLES
communities.title: OTH Communication Ecosystem
communities.summary: OTH communication is a critical, bidirectional capability supporting MALE/HALE aircraft, multi-ship operations, and future missions. It relies on satellite-based infrastructure for military C2, FAA ATC, and sensor data transmission. Technical constraints like higher data rates and wide receiver bandwidth limit range due to noise power increases.

communities.title: Mission Performance Requirements Analysis
communities.summary: The data defines performance envelopes for six UAV mission categories (Long Range, Combat Fighter, Light Civil, Short TO & L, Short/Medium Range, and Class I UAVs) based on maximum lift coefficient ($C_{Lmax}$) and thrust-to-weight ratio ($T/W$). Long Range missions require a range >5400 nm with $C_{Lmax}$ 1.6–2.2 and $T/W$ 0.20–0.35, supporting two distinct goals. Class I UAVs exhibit a broader $T/W$ span (0.20–1.30) compared to other specific missions.

communities.title: Airfoil Selection Analysis
communities.summary: Three airfoil candidates (NACA 0012, NACA 63-418, NACA 63-618) were evaluated under a Mach number of 0.1126 and Reynolds number of 9.5273×10^5. Selection was based on minimizing the effective drag coefficient, resulting in the choice of NACA 63-418.

communities.title: Reynolds Number Calculation Dependencies
communities.summary: The Reynolds number (Re) is a dimensionless quantity characterizing flow regimes, with typical values around $10^6$ but varying significantly based on flight conditions and study parameters. Its calculation depends on four key variables: altitude temperature (T), dynamic viscosity ($\mu$), mean chord length (b), and reference temperature (T0).

communities.title: Boom-Mounted Tail Wing Configuration Analysis
communities.summary: The Boom-Mounted Tail Wing configuration integrates a tail wing boom matching the horizontal tail width, with design parameters like span, diameter, and moment arm derived from structural and aerodynamic constraints similar to traditional wings.

nodes: HEALTH AND STATUS OF THE VEHICLE
REAL TIME OR NEAR REAL TIME VEHICLE POSITION
communities.title: UAV Operational Dependencies in Global Airspace
communities.summary: The community describes the critical dependency of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) operations in Global airspace on Over the Horizon Communications (OTH). OTH is required for situational awareness, command and control, and real-time vehicle positioning. Researchers rely on C2 to monitor instrument health, onboard data recorders, and receive real-time data or snapshots. Positioning relies on both AV navigation systems and GPS satellites.

communities.title: Dropsonde Systems Community Report
communities.summary: The community centers on Dropsonde systems, which are widely used high-altitude aircraft instruments for obtaining atmospheric data and measuring horizontal wind. They utilize unique methods and have seen recent improvements via the NCAR/Vaisala collaboration resulting in smaller, lighter sondes. Future improvements may require advanced GPS technology, which is potentially subject to ITAR restrictions. No directly competing or disruptive technologies are currently known.

communities.title: Military Aviation Technology Transfer and Application
communities.summary: The community describes the transfer of virtually identical technology currently used on other aircraft to UAV platforms and Lagrangian balloons. This technology supports DoD applications requiring autonomous behavior, formation flying, and network-centric communication without anticipated complications.

communities.title: Network-Centric Communication Architecture for Air Operations
communities.summary: The network-centric communication architecture is a C2 and sensor data concept utilizing multiple directional, asymmetric links similar to the Internet. It is designed to enhance civilian UAV operations, manned air vehicle communications, science data flow, and general civilian communications. The architecture functions as a node-based system connecting various entities including satellites, remote C2 locations, unmanned air vehicles (UAVs), manned air vehicles, vehicle payloads, and mission managers.

communities.title: UAV Market and Technology Landscape
communities.summary: The UAV market spans military, civil/commercial, science, and government sectors, utilizing airframe and avionics components. Key technologies include SAR (TRL ~6) and X-band radars for the military, while active radar systems face high cost barriers accessible only to the military. Integrated Systems Health Management (ISHM) is a critical requirement driven by industry standards and government/aerospace company research investments.

nodes: ROLE OF UAVS: A CAPABILITIES ASSESSMENT
TRANSPORT AND CHEM. EVOLUTION IN TROPO.
communities.title: UAV Mission Capabilities and Civil Applications
communities.summary: The data outlines a framework of UAV mission types, including Broad Area Surveillance, Physical Oceanography, Tunnel Detection, and others, categorized under Homeland Security and Earth Sciences. These missions are assessed via weighted capability scores in an output matrix, with specific attention to the applicability of military technology to civil UAVs/UASs.

communities.title: UAVSAR Program and Precision Trajectory Control Community
communities.summary: The UAVSAR program funds precision trajectory control development for the Gulfstream III aircraft to support L-band repeat-pass SAR migration. This technology must achieve better than 5 meters accuracy for interferometric applications, driving maturation of specific systems while other SAR technologies face TRL projection challenges due to lack of current investments.

nodes: IN-SITU DETECTION OF TRACE GASES USING DIFFERENCE FREQUENCY GENERATION LASERS
communities.title: UAV Sensor Ecosystem and Enabling Technologies
communities.summary: The community centers on Sensors as the core enabling technology for UAVs, MAVs, and J-UCAS systems. Key relationships involve dependencies between sensors and critical supporting technologies (models, algorithms, automated reasoning) for machinery monitoring, specific sensor types (e.g., radiometer, lightning, temperature), and platform requirements (weight ~7 lbs, volume ~70 cu in, power ~10 W). Challenges include the need for adaptation of existing imaging systems, downsizing of instrument packaging, and development of accurate in-cloud measurements.

nodes: OPEN ARCHITECTURES AND SYSTEMS FOR COMMAND AND CONTROL
communities.title: Payload Instrumentation Community Report
communities.summary: The payload instrumentation community centers on a suite of sensors including active/passive microwave, SAR, radiometers, and cameras. Key quantitative attributes show conflicting total weight values (80 lbs to 1500 lbs) and power requirements ranging from 1 to 5 kW. Volume is dictated by antenna area (10.8–53.8 ft²), while scanning methods like conical scanning and multi-polarization are desired. Investment rates of $1,000–$2,000/lb suggest weight reduction targets around 100 lbs.

nodes: LIGHT WEIGHT COMPOSITE OVERWRAPPED PRESSURE VESSELS
communities.title: COPV Systems for UAV Propulsion and Space Applications
communities.summary: Composite Overwrapped Pressure Vessels (COPVs) are critical lightweight components for storing hydrogen in high-flying UAVs and space applications like planetary missions. Key challenges include stress rupture, damage tolerance, and reliability over long durations. Material evolution involves transitioning from poorly understood Kevlar fibers to carbon and other advanced fibers.

communities.title: UAV Reliability Framework
communities.summary: The UAV flight system relies on a multi-faceted reliability framework centered on the Flight Control System (FCS), which must never fail catastrophically and must adapt to failures. Key viewpoints for assessing overall reliability include basic onboard system reliability, pilot adaptability, control network integrity, power system stability, and specific FCS reconfiguration capabilities.

communities.title: Remote Payload Instrumentation and Technology Templates
communities.summary: The community consists of a Remote Payload containing various instruments (Lidars, Spectrometers, Profilers) and templates produced by a Technology Working Group for specific detection technologies like sondes and trace gases.

communities.title: UAS Open Architecture & ARC Technologies
communities.summary: The community centers on a new Unmanned Aircraft System (UAV) utilizing an open architecture with plug-and-play capabilities, led by ARC for multiple technology areas. Key features include modular payloads and sensor systems designed for easy replacement by ground maintenance personnel, alongside failure identification/classification to support intelligent contingency management.

communities.title: High-Altitude Aircraft Sensor Platform
communities.summary: The Argus high-altitude aircraft serves as a platform equipped with diverse sensors for meteorological measurements, remote sensing of temperature and water vapor, radar/radiometer systems for precipitation, electrical activity sensors, visible imaging instruments, and surface wave spectra sensors (GPS reflectance, LIDAR). A pod component is required to carry drop-sondes. Conflicting requirements exist regarding the necessity of viewing ports: one source states they are necessary for high-altitude aircraft, while another specifies they are necessary for the system.

communities.title: Airborne SatCom Systems and Frequency Band Utilization
communities.summary: The community centers on airborne satellite communication (SatCom) systems that utilize multiple frequency bands (L, C, S, X, K, KA) for various purposes. These systems employ efficient modulation schemes. Distinct from these are active and passive microwave instruments used for soil moisture measurement, which operate in L and P bands.

communities.title: Quantum 3D Interoperability Gap in Open Architecture Systems
communities.summary: The Navy's Open Architecture (OA) initiative requires integration with manned and unmanned assets, a capability currently lacking in Quantum 3D's solutions. Quantum 3D markets COTS open-architecture IG solutions and embedded visual computing systems for military and aerospace sectors, but these products lack interoperability with other systems. The ARCI-like process is used to facilitate OA introduction in surface combat systems.

communities.title: Sensor Systems on Manned Aircrafts
communities.summary: The community centers on sensor technologies (FTS, GFCR, Hyperspectral) deployed on manned aircrafts for automated operations. Key technical requirements include high sensitivity necessitating low noise HgCdTe detectors and cryogenic cooling, which drive costs. These systems enable vertical mapping of species via pressure broadening effects.

communities.title: UAV Data Processing & Mission Capabilities
communities.summary: The community centers on Intelligent Data Handling and Processing, which encompasses both Onboard and Ground-based processing strategies. High data stream rates create demands that onboard processing mitigates by reducing reliance on high-bandwidth satellite communication (SATCOM). Ground processing utilizes available bandwidth to relay processed data to Mission Control Centers and Mission Planners for decision-making. These capabilities support specific operational objectives including Quick Deployment, Long-Endurance Missions, Multi-Ship Operations, Vehicle Turn-Around, and Civilian UAV Mission Requirements involving rapid turnaround times.

communities.title: Interferometric SAR Monitoring of Geophysical Hazards
communities.summary: INTERFEROMETRIC SAR MEASUREMENTS observe near-field surface deformation across decimeter to hundreds of meters scales, supporting monitoring of VOLCANOES, LANDSLIDES, EARTHQUAKES, and erosion processes. The system complements LIDAR and is carried by UAV platforms to study GEOPHYSICAL PROCESSES in the EARTH'S CRUST.

nodes: CONSTRUCTION OF PLANS INVOLVING COMPLEX RESOURCES
REDUCTION IN ERRORS AND DRUDGERY OVER MANUAL HUMAN PLANNING AND SCHEDULING
communities.title: IMM & ISHM Enabling Technology Community
communities.summary: The community centers on Intelligent Mission Management (IMM) and Intelligent System Health Management (ISHM) as core enabling technologies for UAV operations. These systems facilitate planning, scheduling, and maintenance activities for individual UAVs and fleets, aiming to optimize mission costs and reduce errors compared to manual methods.

nodes: MISSION-REQUIREMENTS DRIVEN PLATFORM AND SYSTEMS CAPABILITIES AND FUNCTIONALITIES (OPERATIONAL MODELS)
communities.title: IVSM and Monitored Execution Framework
communities.summary: The community describes a framework where IVSM relies on mission-requirements driven capabilities, while monitored execution integrates inputs from system sensors, human-controlled ground systems, and IVSM to track progress.

WIND MEASUREMENTS IN PRECIPITATION AND CLOUD REGIONS
communities.title: Payload Sensors Technology Community Report
communities.summary: The community centers on 'PAYLOAD SENSORS' as a primary enabling technology identified by the TWG. It encompasses sub-level technologies including Passive Microwave, Active Microwave, and Active Optical systems. Key attributes include lightweight, low loss, and antenna technology, with specific performance metrics like 65.6 ft penetration depth for high-resolution cameras. Stakeholders include the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the National Science Foundation (NSF). Applications range from distributed sensor configurations to multi-UAV transmit/receive setups and missions of opportunity.

CHEM. DETECTION USING LASER DIODE SPECTROSCOPY
communities.title: CO2 In-Situ Detection Technology Community
communities.summary: The community centers on in-situ detection of carbon dioxide (CO2), utilizing specific sensor technologies such as non-dispersing IR analyzers, laser diode spectroscopy, and microsystems-based chemical sensor arrays. Key enabling technologies include Quantum Cascade Lasers and Quantum Cascade Laser Spectrometers, which are integral to the Sensors CO2 subsystem for direct environmental identification.

nodes: HIGH ALTITUDE LONG ENDURANCE REMOTELY OPERATED AIRCRAFT
LIGHTWEIGHT HYDROGEN-BASED STORAGE AND FEED SYSTEMS

SCIENCE AND AERONAUTICS RESEARCH MISSION DIRECTORATES
communities.title: HALE ROA Technology Community Report
communities.summary: The High Altitude Long Endurance Remotely Operated Aircraft (HALE ROA) program, formerly under AuRA and now part of the Earth Sciences Capability Demonstration sponsored by the Science and Aeronautics Research Mission Directorates, focuses on developing 'perceptive' UAVs with large, flexible wings. Key technical areas include adaptive flight controls, integrated systems management, hydrogen-based fuel cells, and non-conventional propulsion like HPDMS.

nodes: VERIFICATION AND VALIDATION OF AUTONOMY SOFTWARE
communities.title: UAV Intelligent Mission Management Ecosystem
communities.summary: The data defines an ecosystem centered on Intelligent Mission Management (IMM) for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), integrating contingency management, adaptive control, and verification technologies to ensure safety in uncertain environments.

nodes: COMPONENT FAULT DETECTION IDENTIFICATION AND RECOVERY (FDIR)
DATA STORED/TRANSMITTED ON DEMAND FOR ON-GROUND DECISION SUPPORT
communities.title: Intelligent System Health Management (ISHM) Ecosystem
communities.summary: The provided data defines Intelligent System Health Management (ISHM) as a central enabling technology for UAVs, integrating various sub-systems and methods to ensure safety, reliability, and operational support. Key components include Built-in Self Test (BIST), Component Fault Detection Identification and Recovery (FDIR), and System/Vehicle Level FDIR, all contributing to system health assessment and recovery.

communities.title: Solid Oxide Fuel Cell (SOFC) Technology and Components
communities.summary: The data describes Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFC) as high-temperature devices used for energy generation, offering superior efficiency compared to PEM fuel cells in regenerative modes. SOFCs consist of specific material sets for their anode, cathode, electrolyte, and interconnect components. A distinct entry also references operations involving Aerosonde equipment in the Solomon Islands in 2003.

nodes: ENGINEERING OF COMMERCIAL SENSOR FOR UAV APPLICATION
communities.title: Technology Working Groups and Cost Drivers Analysis
communities.summary: The community centers on Technology Working Groups utilizing H.3 Technology Templates, including the Delphi Method for forecasting, to manage operating and development costs. These costs are categorized into operational expenses (staff travel, salary), scale-up, integration, manufacturing, testing, and specific drivers like DFG sensor engineering.

communities.title: Onboard Replanning in ISHM Contexts
communities.summary: The community centers on 'ONBOARD REPLANNING' as a critical capability for maintaining mission safety and efficiency under degraded conditions or environmental hazards like smoke/ash plumes. Key relationships involve dependencies on architecture understanding, mission profile limits, and the specific challenges faced by Mars rovers due to communication lags.

nodes: AUTOMATED IDENTIFICATION OF DEVIATIONS FROM PRESCRIBED OPERATIONS
AUTOMATED IDENTIFICATION OF UNEXPECTED DEVIATIONS FROM THE NORM
MONITORING EACH SUB-SYSTEM FOR ON-CONDITION MAINTENANCE
communities.title: Databases Suite for UAV Operations
communities.summary: The Databases suite enables automated identification of deviations from prescribed operations and unexpected norms for UAVs. It utilizes multivariate statistics, variance metrics, and digitally recorded parameters to extract signatures and identify clusters of typical and atypical data patterns, supporting on-condition maintenance monitoring.

nodes: H.2.3.1 NUMERIC DATA-BASED TECHNOLOGICAL FORECASTING TECHNIQUES
METHODS TO PREDICT FUTURE STATE OF TECHNOLOGY
communities.title: Civil UAV Development Organization Structure and Forecasting Processes
communities.summary: The Civil UAV Development Organization is structured around an Assessment Team, a Steering Committee, Technology Working Groups (including Monitoring, Data Structuring, and Forecasting Support groups), and external partners like the University Space Research Association. The organization utilizes specific forecasting techniques, such as statistical curve fitting within numeric data-based methods, to predict future technology states for mission readiness evaluation, acknowledging inherent uncertainties in these predictions.

communities.title: Polymer Crosslinked Aerogels Technology Assessment
communities.summary: Laboratory-optimized (TRL 3) polymer crosslinked aerogels rely on underlying silica density and specific crosslinking polymers, though current options like epoxies and isocyanates limit temperature stability. Higher-performance alternatives such as polyimides remain at TRL 2, while non-polymer silica aerogels are identified for UAV applications.

communities.title: ALTAIR UAV Community Report
communities.summary: The ALTAIR is a versatile Unmanned Aerial Vehicle developed by General Atomics, featuring triplex avionics and a fault-tolerant flight control system. It supports missions including the ongoing FiRE program (since 2006) and the AMES Fire Mission with NOAA packages. The aircraft has demonstrated an 18-hour endurance and can carry up to 3000 lbs on external wing stations. Development history includes Simonov Design Bureau's involvement starting in 2011, though they were pulled from the project in 2018.

communities.title: Forpost-M and Related Systems Report
communities.summary: The Forpost-M is a strike-capable drone system developed by the Ural Civil Aviation Plant, announced at Army-2015. It is based on the Israeli Searcher platform but utilizes Russian components. A separate variant exists for the Russian Federal Nuclear Center 'Serpukhov-2'. Work on the Altair system was confirmed to continue at the Ural Civil Aviation Plant by Deputy Defense Minister Alexei Krivoruchko in December 2018.

communities.title: XQ-58A Valkyrie Community Report
communities.summary: The XQ-58A Valkyrie is an experimental jet-powered Class III UAV built by Kratos Defense & Security for the US Air Force's Low-Cost Attritable Strike Demonstrator (LCASD), also known as Loyal Wingman. Unveiled in January 2017, it completed its maiden flight at Yuma Proving Grounds in Arizona. The aircraft has an internal payload capacity of 227 kg and can carry two GBU-39 Small Diameter Bombs.

communities.title: Altus UAV Community Report
communities.summary: The Altus aircraft is a civil variant of the U.S. Air Force Predator developed by General Atomics Aeronautical Systems Incorporated for civilian scientific research. It features a nose-mounted payload compartment capable of carrying up to 330 lbs of instruments, including atmospheric sampling sensors. The primary Altus II variant operates with an endurance of about 24 hours and a ceiling of approximately 65,000 ft (19.8 km). A modified version exists equipped with a two-stage turbocharger. Currently, the Altus II resides at NASA Dryden Flight Research Center.

communities.title: General Atomics and UAV Ecosystem
communities.summary: The community centers on General Atomics as a major aircraft and military UAV manufacturer involved in discussions with the DOD regarding the IRIDIUM system. Key entities include the Altus I (first single-stage turbocharger UAV built by GA), the Predator class vehicle (target of INMARSAT capability addition), and L3-COM (associated with TRL 2 technology forecasts). Relationships span manufacturing, program procurement (DOE ARM-UAV), and communication link integration.

nodes: RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT VEHICLE EMBEDDED ANALYSIS ON LINUX (REVEAL)
RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT VEHICLE EMBEDDED ANALYSIS ON LINUX (REVEAL) PROJECT
communities.title: NASA Dryden UAV and Aircraft Experimentation Community
communities.summary: The community centers on NASA Dryden, which hosted early MD-11 engine-only flight experiments following the 1989 Sioux City accident, and managed multiple UAV projects including the NOAA UAS Demonstration Project and the REVEAL project. Key activities involved developing embedded Linux technology and miniaturizing Iridium modem assemblies for micro UAV applications, alongside discussions with L3-COM regarding command and control capabilities.

communities.title: Aerosonde UAV and Heavy-Lift UAV Community Report
communities.summary: The Aerosonde UAV, developed by Aerosonde Pty, Ltd., is a lightweight unmanned aircraft (33 lbs/15 kg) designed for meteorological reconnaissance and environmental monitoring. Its operational ceiling at intermediate weights is 23,000 ft (7 km). In contrast, heavy-lift UAVs (>50 kg) carry modular sensor suites, firefighting equipment, and industrial payloads. Fuel loads for conventionally powered long-endurance vehicles typically range from 40% to 60% of gross takeoff weight. A distinct size class exists for quadcopters sized by Winslow et al., with weights between 30 g and 1 kg.

communities.title: Argus Instrumentation Community Report
communities.summary: The community comprises four primary components for the Argus system: a Main Instrument, a Dewar (with dry ice), a Pre-Water Trap, and a Pump Box Assembly. These units are co-located in a resource summary table [c_43a91fea30e4fa71e9aeea87]. The Main Instrument measures 27.1 x 17.4 x 10.5 inches and weighs 77 lbs, requiring 280W/170W of power [c_43a91fea30e4fa71e9aeea87]. The Dewar has dimensions of 8.0 inches OD x 12.0 inches H, weighs 18 lbs, and includes a relief valve requirement [c_43a91fea30e4fa71e9aeea87]. The Pre-Water Trap measures 23.0 x 2.6 x 3.5 inches [c_43a91fea30e4fa71e9aeea87], while the Pump Box Assembly is 20.0 x 9.5 x 8.25 inches, weighs 33 lbs, and can share hazmat cylinders (4 - 0.7L gas) [c_43a91fea30e4fa71e9aeea87]. All components are interconnected via resource summary listings [c_43a91fea30e4fa71e9aeea87], with the Dewar also noted as a component for Argus on Altair [c_e01b1ca5da0e7ae79aaf8d80].

communities.title: IOLC Technologies and Civilian Applications
communities.summary: The community centers on IOLC technologies developed by the DoD for specific vehicle/sensor configurations, which are unlikely to transition to civilian UAV applications due to limited funding and a lack of capability to meet demanding civilian user requirements. Conversely, graph theoretic tools are identified as relevant for addressing complex cooperation needs in the civilian sector.

communities.title: Critical Phases of UAS Missions
communities.summary: The community defines critical phases for Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) missions where failures may occur. These phases include specific altitude levels, operational environments like populated areas, and ground operations such as pushback.

communities.title: UAV Systems Technology and Operational Landscape
communities.summary: The community centers on Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) evolving from hydrocarbon-based propulsion to hydrogen fuel cells, driven by safety, reliability, and cost reduction needs. Key relationships include the maturity of H2-air PEM fuel cells for near-term UAV use, the role of government in commercial insurance, and the integration challenges in control and signal processing.

communities.title: UAV Power and Propulsion Technology Community
communities.summary: The community centers on power and propulsion technologies enabling UAV missions, contrasting fuel cells with internal combustion engines. Fuel cells offer higher efficiency and lower specific fuel consumption, extending endurance in electric propulsion systems, while internal combustion engines require multiple turbochargers for high-altitude operations. Key sub-technologies include advanced fuel cells, power distribution systems, and motor-driven propellers, though power electronics weight remains a limitation.

communities.title: UAV Structural Health and Payload Vibration Concerns
communities.summary: The community focuses on the intersection of excessive vibration, payload systems with strict pointing requirements, and long-term structural health monitoring for UAVs. As UAV reliability improves, interest grows in utilizing mature health-monitoring technologies to address structural integrity issues exacerbated by vibration.

communities.title: SAR SYSTEMS REQUIREMENTS AND MATURENESS
communities.summary: SAR systems are characterized as mature and simpler technologies compared to IFSAR, operating at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6-7. Key requirements include high-precision antenna placement, formation flights, large data bandwidth, and DC power in the 10 kW range.

communities.title: Reliable Flight Systems Community Report
communities.summary: The community centers on achieving significant improvements in Reliable Flight Systems for UAVs through end-to-end mission spectrum approaches rather than subsystem isolation. Key enablers include software development (3-5 years to maturity), sensor integration, and reconfigurable controller concepts investigated by the US Air Force. Historical context includes the US Army's Aquila UAV program (1979-1987) and DFRC technologies with specific TRL estimates.

communities.title: DFRC Technology Community Report
communities.summary: The Defense Research Center (DFRC) leads testing for Collision Avoidance, Reliable Flight Systems, Over-the-Horizon Comm., and Medium TRL approaches using the Iron Bird simulator. The ARC Inductive Monitoring System (IMS) is a specific example of a Medium TRL approach that learns normal system behavior to predict anomalies.

communities.title: UAV Data Handling Technology Hierarchy
communities.summary: The evidence outlines a hierarchical structure for UAV technologies under 'Intelligent Data Handling & Ground Processing', including sub-levels like Computing and Data Archiving, and further sub-sub-levels such as Real-time Onboard Processing and Data Mining. A system integration issue requiring tight integration is noted, alongside a cost category classification.

communities.title: Li-S Battery Technology Overview
communities.summary: Li-S batteries are a high-energy-density secondary battery system within the Long-life Rechargeable batteries category, projected to achieve 700 Wh/l energy density and 600 Wh/kg specific energy at the cell level. They feature recharge efficiency exceeding 85% and are designed for coupling with solar arrays to manage power during mission eclipses.

communities.title: UAV Air Collision Avoidance Regulatory and Technical Landscape
communities.summary: The National Airspace System currently lacks defined performance levels or a regulatory process for Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAVs). While an integrated program is maturing air collision avoidance capabilities with an estimated cost of roughly $10M, most existing ground collision avoidance systems do not address air collision avoidance. Regulatory requirements regarding air collision avoidance apply to vehicles operating within the national airspace.

communities.title: UAV Technology and Operational Landscape
communities.summary: The community centers on Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAVs) evolving from early WWI concepts to modern applications in atmospheric research, reconnaissance, and civil/defense sectors. Key themes include the necessity for advanced autonomy (Level-0 to Level-2 processing), collision avoidance systems (CAS), and regulatory integration into the National Airspace System (NAS). Significant technological gaps exist in miniaturized lidar, robust compact instruments, and carbon nano-fiber composites. Operational constraints involve Beyond Line of Sight (BLOS) communications, ITAR regulations for specific payload/range thresholds, and high costs associated with flight testing.

communities.title: Global UAV Inventory and Deployment Analysis
communities.summary: The data outlines a global UAV ecosystem where the U.S. is the primary exporter, with active inventories comprising 171 types and infrastructure spanning 61 countries. Key focus areas include next-generation designs (swarms, stealthy aircraft) explored by at least seven nations, and specific deployments such as MQ-1C Gray Eagles in Cameroon and Reapers in Niger.

communities.title: Offshore Data Gathering and Intelligent Handling
communities.summary: The community describes an operational framework for gathering massive datasets via UAVs from 25 to 110 nm offshore, necessitating intelligent data handling through automation and autonomous analysis systems.

communities.title: FAA, NAS, and UAV Regulatory Framework
communities.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) leads efforts to integrate Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) into the National Airspace System (NAS), managing certification processes, issuing Certificates of Authorization (COAs), and enforcing flight restrictions. Key initiatives include Special Committee 203 for safety standards and Access 5 for seamless integration goals.

communities.title: ON-BOARD INTELLIGENCE AND SYSTEM RELIABILITY
communities.summary: 시스템 신뢰성을 개선하기 위해 중복성 증가, 온보드 지능 추가, 그리고 자체 파괴 방법 등 다양한 접근법이 존재하며, 이들은 초기 비용과 지속적인 무게 페널티를 공유합니다.

communities.title: Weather Focus Mission Community Report
communities.summary: The Weather Focus Mission is a research initiative designed to enhance weather forecasting and augment satellite data. Its scope includes specific research elements such as Atmospheric Rivers and THORPEX, alongside operational components like the NOAA/NCEP Winter Storms Program. The mission utilizes satellites GIFTS and GPM for validation purposes.

communities.title: Japan UAV and Technology Community Report
communities.summary: The community centers on Japan's advanced UAV ecosystem, featuring models like the FFOS/FFRS (Fuji Heavy Industries) and JUXS-S1 (Hitachi), alongside strategic infrastructure at Yokota Air Base and Marjan Airstrip. The nation actively pursues SOFC programs for energy and autonomous helicopter projects.

communities.title: Operation Southern Watch and Surveillance Assets
communities.summary: Operation Southern Watch was a U.S. campaign following the First Gulf War to monitor Iraqi military movements in southern Iraq and enforce a no-fly zone from 1998 until 2003. The operation utilized Desert Hawk small surveillance drones (also known as the Force Protection Airborne Surveillance System) deployed for security at air bases in Kuwait, as well as Air Force RQ-1 Predators.

communities.title: Predator Operations and Missions
communities.summary: The data outlines the operational history of U.S. Predators and Reapers, detailing their deployment to Uzbekistan in 2013 by the CIA for intelligence and strike missions in the Sahel region, as well as participation in counter-terrorism, counter-crime, and counter-insurgency operations. Specific missions include the 'Summer Project' targeting Osama bin Laden and support for French counter-terrorism efforts in Mali.

communities.title: RQ-4A Global Hawk and Unmanned Reconnaissance Unit in 2003
communities.summary: In 2003, the RQ-4A Global Hawk reached serial production and was employed in Operation Iraqi Freedom, where its intelligence contributed to destroying 13 air defense missile batteries, 50 surface-to-air missile launchers, and 300 tanks. A study by Forecast International indicated that U.S. spending on UAVs accounted for approximately 73% of worldwide research and production spending that year. Concurrently, an Unmanned Reconnaissance Company was activated in 2003 and located at Prostějov.

communities.title: Electric Multirotor Sizing Tool (EMST) and Propulsion Characteristics
communities.summary: The Electric Multirotor Sizing Tool (EMST), developed by Bershadsky and Haviland, utilizes parameterized propulsion characteristics such as torque, KV rating, and battery internal resistance to meet target thrust and endurance levels. However, the tool's capability is limited by external inputs including airframe mass, structural factors, system-level correlations, and specific sizing metrics like power drawn and takeoff distance reduction parameters studied by Kotarski et al.

communities.title: Global Unmanned Aircraft Operations and Technical Characteristics
communities.summary: The community describes the operational deployment of unmanned aircraft across multiple nations, including Ukraine, Russia, and Mexico, alongside technical parameters such as drag prediction methods and takeoff distance constraints. Key findings highlight the rising use of consumer-grade drones in eastern Ukraine, their countermeasures, and specific engineering factors like wing area affecting performance.

communities.title: Border Monitoring Mission Community Report
communities.summary: The Border Monitoring Mission encompasses land, maritime/coastal borders, and associated airspace to detect unauthorized entry by immigration and customs violators.

communities.title: UAV Data Transmission and Bandwidth Requirements
communities.summary: The community describes the relationship between data transmission for UAV operations, its associated bandwidth requirements, and the role of autonomy levels in mitigating these requirements.

communities.title: Lidar Miniaturization Technologies and Constraints
communities.summary: Emerging laser technologies, specifically fiber lasers and new diode laser designs, are addressing critical size, weight, and power consumption limitations in lidar systems. Conversely, traditional gas cell configurations like the Herriot cell and White cell contribute to bulkiness, hindering miniaturization efforts.

communities.title: Radar Digital Receiver Development and FPGA Integration
communities.summary: The community centers on the development of radar digital receivers utilizing recent field-programmable gate array (FPGA) chips to reduce size, weight, and power consumption. Current industry solutions lack specific tailoring for specialized radar systems operating in cloud conditions or precipitation.

communities.title: Trace Gas Detection Technologies and Applications
communities.summary: The community describes advanced in-situ detection methods for trace gases, utilizing optical feedback and cavity enhanced absorption spectroscopy in the near-infrared, as well as difference frequency generation (DFG) lasers in the mid-infrared. These techniques measure isotopic composition and are applied in atmospheric and meteorological research missions on UAVs.

communities.title: Advanced Human-Machine Interaction Systems
communities.summary: The community describes a missing supporting technology for advanced outer-loop management systems, focusing on modalities of interaction between humans and these systems. Key examples include natural language interfaces used with UAVs, which are currently characterized as very sketchy.

nodes: CENTER FOR INTERDISCIPLINARY REMOTELY-PILOTED AIRCRAFT STUDIES
communities.title: CENTER FOR INTERDISCIPLINARY REMOTELY-PILOTED AIRCRAFT STUDIES
communities.summary: The Center for Interdisciplinary Remotely-Piloted Aircraft Studies (CIRPAS), established by the Office of Naval Research in spring 1996 at the Naval Postgraduate School, manages UAV programs, provides access to manned aircraft, support equipment, and scientific instruments, and develops instrumentation for radar demonstrations.

nodes: HIGH PWR DENSITY PROPULSOIN USING HIGH TEMP. SUPERCONDUCTOR MOTORS
communities.title: Aircraft Propulsion System Configuration Analysis
communities.summary: The data outlines aircraft propulsion systems categorized by shape (Pusher, Tractor, Push-pull, Wing-mounted) and power source (Electric vs. Internal Combustion). A specific electric configuration (Case4) utilizes a Tiger Motor U15II 80KV motor, G40*13.1 propeller, Thunder 1224S ESC, and LiPo batteries. Table 7-1 defines these shapes across six configurations, noting that Pusher is dominant (80% of cases) while Tractor accounts for 14%. Quantitative data includes component weights: 8 motors totaling 13.92 kg, 8 propellers at 1.896 kg, and 2 batteries at 24.86 kg.

communities.title: 무인기체 착륙장치 부재 분석
communities.summary: 분석 결과, 총 91 건 (39%) 의 사례에서 착륙장치가 사용되지 않는 'NONE' 카테고리가 확인되었으며, 이는 Fledermaus, Kapothaka, Mucke 등 다양한 무인기체가 기술 개발 단계에 머물렀거나 상업화에 실패한 경우와 관련이 있습니다.

communities.title: Aircraft Landing Gear Configurations
communities.summary: 초기 구성 (Initial Configuration) 은 랜딩 기어 (Landing Gear) 의 주요 구성 요소로, 트라이시클 (Tricycle) 방식이 가장 흔하게 사용되며 (56%), 바이시클 (Bicycle), 스키드 (Skid) 등 다양한 형태가 존재합니다. 랜딩 기어는 수납식 (Retractable) 또는 고정식 (Fixed) 방식으로 분류됩니다.

communities.title: 항공기 설계 데이터 분석 요약
communities.summary: 제공된 증거에 따르면, 최대 이륙 중량 (MTOW) 기반 주요 형상 분석에서 총 235 개의 구성이 기록되었습니다. 가장 지배적인 형태는 단엽기 (MONO PLANE) 로 207 회 (약 88%) 를 차지하며, 그 다음으로 델타 날개 (DELTA) 가 17 회입니다. 비행 정제 (flight regime) 분석에서는 서브소닉 (SUB SONIC) 이 208 회로 압도적으로 많으며, 초음속 (HYPERSONIC) 은 7 회, 하이퍼소닉은 3 회 등 소수만 기록되었습니다. 양날개 (BIPLANE) 와 비행선 (FLYING BOAT) 은 분석에서 0 회로 나타나지 않았습니다.

communities.title: 32nd Regiment and Associated UAV Operations
communities.summary: The 32nd Regiment, a British military unit deployed to Shaibah Air Base in November 2003 with operations continuing until 2009, comprised the 22nd, 18th, 57th, and 46th (HQ) Batteries. It provided ISR support to Multi-National Division South East using Phoenix and Desert Hawk 1 UAVs, alongside leased Hermes 450 aircraft. The regiment was scheduled for disbandment in 2021 under the Army 2020 Restructuring Plan, with UAV operations shifting to the 47th Regiment.

communities.title: UAV Configuration Analysis: Monoplane Dominance and Case Variants
communities.summary: The data describes a community of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) configurations, primarily focusing on the 'Monoplane' main wing type which accounts for 88% of cases. Six specific case studies (Cases 2-6) are detailed, each utilizing a Monoplane configuration with Tricycle Landing Gear. Variations exist in tail mounting (Conventional vs. Boom-mounted), engine placement (Tractor vs. Pusher), and initial value estimates (ranging from 3.8 to 3.9).

communities.title: Tail Wing Configuration Analysis
communities.summary: The evidence details a community of aircraft tail wing configurations, primarily focusing on the 'Conventional' and 'V-Tail' types within Case 4. It quantifies usage instances for various shapes (e.g., Conventional: 47, V-Tail: 31) and defines specific vertical and horizontal tail volume ratio scaling values for different configurations (e.g., V-tail ratios of 1.00). Relationships map these tail shapes to associated fuselage categories like 'Canard' or 'X-TAIL'.

communities.title: UAV Earth Science Missions and Capability Analysis
communities.summary: The community consists of UAV missions classified as Earth Science objectives, including Cloud Microphysics/Properties, Snow - Liquid Water Equivalents, Cloud Properties, Magnetic Fields Measurements, and River Discharge. These missions are categorized within an output matrix (Table 2.2) and associated with UAV market forecasts. Specific capability scores (0-5) are provided for distinct missions like C.1.19 and C.1.18, detailing performance in areas such as airspace access, endurance, and multi-ship operations.
